name: Larry Klein
title: Mayor of Sunnyvale
background: Klein is the sitting Mayor of Sunnyvale. Per Wikipedia's Sunnyvale, California article, Sunnyvale has directly elected its Mayor to a four-year term in a citywide election since November 2020 (before that, the mayorship rotated among sitting councilmembers), which is why this profile does not list a district: the office Klein holds is elected at-large, not by district.

Klein is the filer and lead signer of the primary arguments in favor of all three City Charter amendments Sunnyvale voters face on the November 2026 ballot: Measure G (letting the City Council authorize alternative public-works contracting methods, such as design-build, beyond the current Charter-mandated lowest-bid system), Measure H (letting the City Council set by ordinance the dollar ceiling on the City Manager's authority to settle legal claims against the City, replacing a $50,000 state-law default unchanged since 1989), and Measure I (extending how long a Council appointee filling a vacant seat serves before facing an election). He also filed rebuttals to the primary arguments in favor of Measures G and I. Full detail on each measure, including their City Attorney Impartial Analyses, fiscal narratives, and the arguments for and against, is covered in content/measures/scc-measure-g-2026.json, scc-measure-h-2026.json, and scc-measure-i-2026.json and not duplicated here.

All three measures originated from the same multi-year Sunnyvale Charter Review Committee process and were placed on the ballot together by a unanimous 7-0 City Council vote on June 23, 2026, following spring 2026 polling (by FM3, of roughly 600 likely voters) that Council reviewed alongside a proposed Council pay-raise measure the polling found consistently under 50% support and which Council deferred rather than placing on the ballot. Klein's arguments in favor of Measures G and I are co-signed by Vice Mayor Richard Mehlinger and other sitting or former Sunnyvale officials; no outside advocacy organization or business group is listed as a filer or signer of any of the three favor arguments in the sources reviewed. A joint campaign website, www.YES-on-GHI.com, covers all three measures together per the rebuttals' own text, though no corresponding FPPC or Cal-Access committee filing was located in the sources reviewed.

I was not able to independently verify Klein's pre-council career, education, prior public offices, the year he first joined the Council or became Mayor, committee assignments, or specific named votes beyond his sponsorship of Measures G, H, and I. This session's WebSearch tool had exhausted its query budget and firecrawl had exhausted its credit budget before this profile was researched, and direct WebFetch attempts at the City of Sunnyvale's official mayor and council pages (sunnyvale.ca.gov) returned 403 Forbidden responses throughout this session; Wikipedia's Sunnyvale, California article names him as the current Mayor but provides no biographical text beyond that. Because of that, years_of_service, committee_memberships, and endorsements_received are left empty or omitted below rather than populated with unverified claims.
voting_record_highlights: Measure G (2026), City of Sunnyvale public-works Charter amendment: Klein was the filer and lead author of the primary argument in favor and its rebuttal; the City Council voted unanimously (7-0) on June 23, 2026 to place Measures G, H, and I on the November 2026 ballot. (Source: City of Sunnyvale City Attorney's Impartial Analysis of Measure G; Citizen Portal, 'Sunnyvale council places three charter amendments on November ballot after weeks of review.')

Measure H (2026), City of Sunnyvale City Manager claim-settlement authority: Klein was the filer and signer of the primary argument in favor, which references the Council having separately adopted, in July 2026, a companion ordinance setting the City Manager's settlement authority at $250,000 contingent on the measure passing. (Source: Measure H primary argument in favor; City of Sunnyvale Report to Council RTC No. 26-0699.)

Measure I (2026), City of Sunnyvale Council-vacancy timing amendment: Klein was the filer and lead author of the primary argument in favor and the rebuttal to the primary argument against, filed by resident Stephen Scandalis. (Source: City of Sunnyvale City Attorney's Impartial Analysis of Measure I.)
attendance: No individually published meeting-attendance or voting-participation record for Mayor Klein was found. The City of Sunnyvale does not appear to publish a per-member attendance scorecard on its public-facing pages; City Council meeting minutes and agendas are available via the city's Legistar-based system, which would in principle allow a manual tally of attendance and votes, but compiling that was not feasible within this session's tool budget (WebSearch and firecrawl both exhausted, and direct fetches of sunnyvale.ca.gov returned 403 Forbidden throughout this session).
